olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Rectangles $BCC_1B_2$, $CAA_1C_2$, $ABB_1A_2$ erected outside acute $\triangle ABC$ with $\angle BC_1C+\angle CA_1A+\angle AB_1B=180^\circ$. Prove lines $B_1C_2$, $C_1A_2$, $A_1B_2$ are concurrent.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 2021

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: The Planar National Park has junctions connected by trails (each junction has degree 3, no trail connects a junction to itself, trails only meet at junctions). A visitor alternates left and right turns until returning to start. What is the largest number of times she could enter any junction?
figure_description: A planar graph showing junctions and trails
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 2021

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: For $n\geq 2$, an $n\times n$ board. Each minute: (i) place a stone in each cell of an L-tromino region with no stones; (ii) if all cells in a column have a stone, remove all; (iii) same for a row. For which $n$ is it possible that after finitely many moves the board has no stones?
figure_description: An L-shaped tromino of three cells
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 2021

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: A finite set $S$ of positive integers: for each $s\in S$ and divisor $d$ of $s$, there is a unique $t\in S$ with $\gcd(s,t)=d$. Find all possible values for $|S|$.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 2021

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Find all positive real solutions to the system of $2n$ equations (for $n\geq 4$): $a_1=\frac{1}{a_{2n}}+\frac{1}{a_2}$, $a_2=a_1+a_3$, $a_3=\frac{1}{a_2}+\frac{1}{a_4}$, $a_4=a_3+a_5$, etc., cyclically.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 2021

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Convex hexagon $ABCDEF$ with $AB\parallel DE$, $BC\parallel EF$, $CD\parallel FA$, and $AB\cdot DE=BC\cdot EF=CD\cdot FA$. $X,Y,Z$ = midpoints of $AD,BE,CF$. Prove the circumcenter of $\triangle ACE$, circumcenter of $\triangle BDF$, and orthocenter of $\triangle XYZ$ are collinear.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 2021
